title: Goal-Anchored Off-Diagonal Trajectory Product VQ for Action-Conditioned Planning
hook: At a fixed actual-byte ceiling, fit a shared additive/product weight codebook from the quantized model's paired predicted rollouts: preserve the original DINO-WM objective directly, then test whether a goal-anchored off-diagonal trajectory relation adds held-out planner fidelity beyond pointwise VQ and ordinary relational quantization.
hook_shape_rationale: The candidate changes the VQ fitting signal while keeping the runtime packed representation and byte ceiling fixed. This is a conditional, mechanism-first weight-compression hypothesis; ordinary RKD and QATMA/TPSD (CR-QAT label) are explicit collision baselines, so no broad novelty is claimed.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved leaf preserves the pairwise geometry of imagined action trajectories while fitting a packed weight codebook, so a low vector-reconstruction error need not preserve the planner's relative candidate structure — stakes: a deployment engineer can lose action choices at the same nominal bytes, while researchers can mistake pointwise fidelity for decision fidelity and draw non-transferring conclusions.
gap_closure.how_closed: Replace only the offline codebook-entry fitting objective: fixed-index additive/product VQ entries are updated from the Q model's paired rollout outputs, the unchanged source planner objective J, and an auxiliary goal-anchored unnormalized off-diagonal Gram B. The runtime lookup layout, group map and actual-byte ceiling stay fixed. This does not claim that relations plus quantization are new; ordinary RKD (CVPR 2019) and QATMA/TPSD (CR-QAT label) (arxiv:2603.05964) are required matched baselines.

core_mechanism: Use the local DINO-WM Wall FP32 reference and its source objective function. For episode e and fixed action probe k, run paired rollout_P(o_e,a_e,k) for P in {F,Q}; the Q rollout is the only source of quantization-dependent trajectory values. Compute J^P(e,k) by calling reproduction/dino-wm-wall/source/planning/objectives.py create_objective_fn(alpha,base,mode) exactly as CEMPlanner does; keep mode=last or mode=all, alpha, base, goal encoding, shape broadcasting, sort and elite update frozen. Separately form auxiliary r^P(e,k) from the same predicted visual/proprio outputs with CAL-frozen pooling/flattening/normalization and target g^r(e) in the same source output coordinate. Set u^P=r^P-g^r, B^P(i,j)=u_i^T u_j and G^P(i,j)=B^P(i,j)/(||u_i||||u_j||+epsilon) only for i != j. B is the unnormalized goal-centered Gram; G is diagnostic and its diagonal is near one, whereas B's diagonal is ||u||^2. Define L_abs=mean||r^Q-r^F||^2+beta_J mean(J^Q-J^F)^2, L_off=mean_{i!=j}(B^Q-B^F)^2 and L_TR=L_abs+lambda_rel L_off. For a predeclared weight block b, represent w_hat(b,m)=sum_r C(b,r)[q(b,m,r)] using the fixed VPTQ/AQLM-compatible packed layout. Freeze all indices. Backpropagate L_TR directly through gather and Q rollout into shared codebook entries with Adam; no STE or closed-form least-squares claim. At most 200 optimizer steps per fit, K<=8 paired probes per batch and H=5, at least two fit seeds. Freeze a common fit-step/data budget after single-A100-40GB forward/backward smoke so collection, all required controls, fits, evaluation and failures fit <=16 allocated GPU-hours. If the minimum fair workload cannot fit or optimize meaningfully, label resource/optimization-inconclusive; no per-vector rollout index search. Use one common actual-byte ceiling C_bytes and report every variant's bytes, overhead and slack. The proposed mechanism is only the conditional question of whether the shared codeword coupling plus this Q-rollout auxiliary objective adds planner fidelity over ordinary RKD-style VQ, QATMA/TPSD (CR-QAT label)-style pairwise similarity quantization, scalar quantization and independent-codebook VQ.
core_mechanism_reasoning: PREMISES: P1 — the original DINO-WM objective_fn and CEM5 screen path can be called without changing the planner; the exact source objective is an implementation anchor, not an asserted result. P2 — paired FP32/Q rollouts can share initial observation, goal, fixed action probe and RNG; this must be checked by a no-op replay before fitting. P3 — auxiliary predicted visual/proprio outputs have a stable CAL-frozen coordinate in which an absolute anchor and goal target are meaningful; this is an untested premise. P4 — an off-diagonal relation between Q predicted rollouts may carry held-out action-neighborhood information beyond the actual planner score J and its goal-score/diagonal component; this is the load-bearing falsification target. P5 — shared codewords may couple vector-group errors differently from scalar and independent-codebook controls at one byte ceiling; this is untested. ESTIMAND: the CAL objective L_TR and the held-out difference in planner first-action agreement, original objective ordering, off-diagonal B error and closed-loop return/success between L_abs+L_off and its matched controls. NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT: fitting a fixed-index codebook to weight/vector MSE, or computing a Gram from fixed actions before Q forward, does not make the target action-conditioned; it cannot test the proposed mechanism. A second naive version uses a cosine Gram without an absolute/source-score anchor; it has rotation/translation ambiguity and a diagonal near one. The candidate adds the original objective J, absolute source-coordinate r anchor, and off-diagonal-only B. DIRECT-COLLISION AUDIT: ordinary RKD and QATMA/TPSD (CR-QAT label) already combine representation relations and quantization; if same paired outputs, goal anchor, byte ceiling and target make them mathematically equivalent, the result is a domain-adaptation hypothesis or negative result. RSAVQ's FIM/natural-gradient projection and channel allocation, QuantWAMs' joint Fisher/reachable-state schedule, MotionVQ's execution-state precision/centroid reuse/custom accelerator, and old RankCal/OTC single-site recipes are excluded from the claimed mechanism.
core_mechanism_steps: Freeze FP32 DINO-WM Wall checkpoint/source and the verified CEM5 SCREEN configuration: horizon=5, topk=30, num_samples=300, var_scale=1, opt_steps=5; call the source objective_fn unchanged. Record the exact mode, alpha, base, tie rule and warm-start/early-stop policy in an implementation manifest.

Pre-register CAL, DEV and TEST episode/task/initial-state splits and paired action probes. Record common random numbers and use the same initial state/goal for FP32 and Q rollouts. The independent units are episodes/tasks/initial states and quantizer-fit seeds; frames, horizons, probes and pairs are not extra n.

Choose an auxiliary r from predicted visual/proprio outputs and a frozen goal target g^r in the same source output coordinate. Freeze pooling, flattening, channel normalization, epsilon, beta_J and lambda_rel before CAL. Call the original objective_fn for J rather than treating r pooling as the CEM definition.

Register the fixed weight vector grouping, additive/product codebook count, index bits, codebook dtype, block map and actual-byte ceiling C_bytes. Initialize indices and entries with the VPTQ-like/local-MSE baseline; report bytes for codebook, indices, scales, metadata, padding and unquantized parameters, plus ceiling slack.

Freeze all indices. Backpropagate L_TR directly through gather and Q rollout into shared codebook entries with Adam; no STE or closed-form least-squares claim. At most 200 optimizer steps per fit, K<=8 paired probes per batch and H=5, at least two fit seeds. Freeze a common fit-step/data budget after single-A100-40GB forward/backward smoke so collection, all required controls, fits, evaluation and failures fit <=16 allocated GPU-hours. If the minimum fair workload cannot fit or optimize meaningfully, label resource/optimization-inconclusive; no per-vector rollout index search.

Optionally test one block-local index shortlist using cached block alternatives and index_steps=1 only after the codebook-only screen; label it secondary and do not use it to rescue a failed primary mechanism.

Run matched variants under the same C_bytes ceiling: FP32 numerical reference; VPTQ-like/local-MSE VQ; L_abs only with lambda_rel=0; L_TR; ordinary RKD-style VQ with same paired r/g^r and relation target; QATMA/TPSD (CR-QAT label)-style pairwise-similarity baseline if the adapter is runnable; same-target scalar; and independent-codebook VQ. Report actual bytes/slack, not nominal-bit equality.

On DEV choose whether to retain the pre-registered positive lambda_rel or stop; do not refit C or q. On TEST freeze one map per fit seed and report original J ordering, first-action agreement, held-out off-diagonal B/G error, and closed-loop return/success with common random numbers.

Separate fake/logical quant from native deployment. Only a real packed loader/kernel can support native checkpoint bytes, peak VRAM, synchronized throughput and control frequency; no custom accelerator or MotionVQ speedup is claimed.

Stop if L_TR has no consistent held-out direction across fit seeds, if off-diagonal gain disappears against goal-score/diagonal-only, if stratified pair shuffle matches the original relation target, if scalar/independent-codebook matches, or if the fixed-byte accounting cannot be met.
falsification_prediction: The conditional prediction is that, after fixed-index codebook-only fitting, L_abs+L_off at one actual-byte ceiling will improve or preserve held-out original-objective ordering and planner first-action agreement, and then closed-loop return/success, relative to L_abs, VPTQ-like/local-MSE and same-target scalar/independent-codebook controls. The gain must also appear in held-out off-diagonal B error and persist across at least two fit seeds; no significance or power claim is made. The load-bearing variable is lambda_rel, including its zero removal control. Goal-score/diagonal-only tests whether off-diagonal is redundant; within-stratum pair-label shuffle preserves episode, horizon, task and action-magnitude marginals while breaking relation; ordinary RKD-style VQ and QATMA/TPSD (CR-QAT label)-style pairwise similarity test direct collision; scalar and independent-codebook test shared-codeword necessity. If any control matches, if only intermediate relation improves without planner endpoint, if Q rollouts were not used for entry updates, or if codebook-only updates cannot meet the byte ceiling, the candidate is no-go or a domain-adaptation/negative result.
compute_budget: Planning estimate only, not measured: codebook-only DINO-WM pilot about 8-16 allocated A100-hours, with 40GB as conservative batch configuration and 80GB as a separate optional check; at most four concurrent A100 jobs. The cap assumes four CAL trajectory batches per update, two entry updates and a small paired DEV/TEST screen, not exhaustive per-index search. If memory, rollout count or actual-byte accounting exceeds the cap, stop. No native kernel or model retraining is included. New paid connector/API budget is $0.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: RSAVQ couples product VQ to language-loss FIM/Riemannian natural-gradient error-direction projection and channel-curvature bit allocation; this candidate fixes the byte map and uses Q predicted action-conditioned rollouts plus the unchanged planner objective and auxiliary off-diagonal relation. The difference remains conditional and must survive direct collision review.

AQLM uses additive codebooks and block-level output reconstruction; this candidate keeps the additive representation but changes the calibration object to paired Q rollouts and an auxiliary goal-anchored relation, with no claim of a new packed format.

VPTQ supplies practical low-bit vector codebooks, indices and packed inference; it is the storage/runtime baseline. This candidate fixes its layout and asks whether codebook entries trained from planner-linked Q rollouts add value.

VQ-VLA is an action tokenizer/residual VQ-VAE and does not compress backbone weights. It remains an adjacent representation baseline, so action-tokenizer gains cannot be reported as parameter compression.

VQVLA/MotionVQ uses execution-state motion-aware precision, centroid reuse and custom accelerator co-design. This candidate has fixed precision/map, no motion schedule, no centroid reuse and no accelerator claim.

QuantWAMs uses joint video-action Fisher and reachable-state/denoising schedule audits; this candidate does not use Fisher or schedule allocation and instead tests fixed-map codebook entries against paired planner rollouts.

Ordinary RKD is a strong direct baseline: use the same paired predicted representations, same frozen goal anchor, same relation target, fixed indices/bytes and fixed codebook layout. If it is mathematically equivalent or ties the candidate, label this a domain-adaptation hypothesis rather than a new optimization.

QATMA/TPSD (CR-QAT label) is a direct quantization collision because it uses pairwise similarity matrices with quantization-aware training. Run or mark unavailable with an evidence record; do not claim novelty until the same-byte goal-anchored comparison is made.

what_step_was_missed: The closest collision already pairs quantization with pairwise similarity; any residual claim must isolate the narrow weight-VQ mechanism: fixed indices in the first pilot, shared codeword coupling, original planner objective kept intact, Q predicted rollout relation as the auxiliary target, fixed actual-byte ceiling and direct RKD/QATMA/TPSD (CR-QAT label) controls. Without that isolation, the candidate is an application adaptation, not a new relation-plus-quantization principle.
